clue.text: Yellow closing in on an equaliser, say?

definitions.meaning: on the London Monopoly board this square sits in the yellow colour group

definitions.text: closing in on an equaliser, say?
definitions.meaning: Leicester City getting the score level, i.e. making the game square

explanation.surface: A football commentator describes a team in yellow pressing for a late equalising goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is the London Monopoly board, so colours define properties. LEICESTER SQUARE is a square in London's West End; read as a sports phrase it is Leicester (the football club) drawing level.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly property sets are named by colour, and this one is coloured yellow; squaring a match means equalising.

clue.text: Blue finds The Guardian is not good, with nothing to write about

parts.note: taken as written
a guardian angel watches over someone
taken as written

indicators.note: to write a word about is to set it down the other way round, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Someone finds the newspaper unsatisfying because it gives them nothing to write about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Guardian' looks like the newspaper but is two pieces. 'to write about' turns the not-good-nothing run round. On the London Monopoly board this property is light blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly sets are named by colour, and this Islington property belongs to the light blue group.

clue.text: Picture that's binding publication

indicators.note: the abbreviation for 'that is' wraps round, binding, the other piece

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, 'that is'
a mag is a magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: A picture is bound into a printed publication.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Free to put in cheque of US sport

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Free to put in cheque of US sport (8)': RID in GIRO gives GRIDIRO, one letter short of GRIDIRON; no clue word supplies the final N, so the clue looks misprinted or misread and no scan or search gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Free to put in cheque of US sport

clue.text: Number of red 7s in the main?

definitions.text: Number of red 7s in the main?

parts.words: Number of red 7s in the main?
parts.note: 7 is STREET, so red streets on the Monopoly board, counted as several; and the number of groups of ships on the sea, the main

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how many red sevens there are in the main part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 7-down gives STREET, and Fleet Street is red on the London Monopoly board, so 'red 7s' suggests the plural of Fleet; 'the main' is the sea, where navies sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of warships at sea are counted as naval squadrons; the main is an old word for the open ocean.

clue.text: Pink bit — say it again? Pink, brown, red, green, yellow, orange and blues

parts.note: a whit is a tiny bit
'eh?' is what you say when you want something repeated

parts.words: Pink, brown, red, green, yellow, orange and blues
parts.note: the colour groups of the Monopoly board listed together make up all of them

explanation.surface: A long list of colours, with someone asking for part of it to be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Pink' is the definition (a pink Monopoly property); the second starts the list of every colour group, which together give ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: On the London Monopoly board this government street belongs to the pink colour group.

clue.text: See 22
Brown or otherwise, man given terrible ordeal

parts.note: the alternative to brown bread or sugar is the white kind
a chap is a man

indicators.note: a terrible ordeal is a messed-up one, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man, brown or not, has been through a terrible ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges ORDEAL to ELROAD. 'or otherwise' asks for brown's usual alternative, as in bread or sugar: WHITE. The property is brown on the London Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly sets are named by colour, and this East London road is in the cheap brown group.

clue.text: Passing time, student put on record by The Edge

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a hem is the edge of a garment
an era is a period of time
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student puts some time into a record made with U2's guitarist The Edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edge is U2's guitarist, which fits 'record', but here it is only a garment's edge. 'put on' sets the time and student pieces after the record and edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral lasts only briefly, like a passing fashion.

clue.text: A horrifying problem?

parts.note: a snag, read also as the nickname of the director famed for horror and suspense films

explanation.surface: Someone describes a problem as horrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Hitchcock, master of suspense, was known as 'Hitch', so a problem named after him would be horrifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or temporary difficulty.

clue.text: About to get put to death, though reformed

parts.note: C is circa, about
hanged means executed on the gallows

explanation.surface: A criminal is about to be executed, despite having reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reformed has altered their ways.

clue.text: Petition to expel Church from ballet movement

indicators.note: to expel is to throw out, so these letters leave the ballet word

parts.note: an entrechat is a ballet leap with the feet crossing in the air

explanation.surface: A petition calls for the Church to be expelled from a ballet movement.
explanation.walkthrough: An ENTRECHAT is a ballet jump in which the dancer beats the feet together.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead, as a petition does.

clue.text: No time for view — oh well

indicators.note: 'no time' means the time letter is dropped

parts.note: a sight is a view

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to having no time for the view says 'oh well'.
explanation.definitionFit: An 'oh well' is an exhalation of resignation.

clue.text: Man parting to script novel that's artificial

indicators.note: the man word parts the rearranged letters, going between them
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: he is a man

explanation.surface: A man is parted from his script for a novel that turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges TO SCRIPT to PROSTTIC, and 'parting' splits that after its fifth letter for the man word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthetic limb is an artificial one.

clue.text: See 2
Instinct about bad returns for US author

indicators.note: returns means the whole assembly comes back the other way
the instinct word goes about the bad word

parts.note: a nose is an instinct, a nose for news
ill means bad

explanation.surface: An American writer's instinct for bad things keeps coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes NOSILLE, and 'returns' turns it round. Ralph Ellison wrote Invisible Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Ellison was the American novelist of Invisible Man.

clue.text: Volcanic crater where a flaming resinous substance forced back

indicators.note: forced back means the run of pieces is pushed into reverse order

parts.note: flaming red is fiery red
lac is a resinous secretion of insects used for shellac

explanation.surface: Flaming resin is forced back out of a volcanic crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced back' reads the run ARE DLAC... backwards as a whole, giving CALDERA from A, flaming and the resin.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large basin formed when a volcano collapses.

clue.text: Crosswords aren't so ignorant

definitions.meaning: a crossword always has clues, so it is never without them

explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a clue lacks knowledge; a puzzle without clues would lack its hints.

clue.text: What spreads half through War and Peace, perhaps

indicators.note: the half word goes through the long-story word

parts.note: War and Peace is an example of an epic, a long novel
demi- means half

explanation.surface: Something spreads through half of War and Peace.
explanation.walkthrough: War and Peace is a classic example of a long novel; the half word goes inside after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a disease outbreak that spreads widely.

clue.text: Shady 3 between Texas and The Commitments

indicators.note: between means the picture word sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: Texas is a state of the US, abbreviated S plus US
IOUs are written commitments to pay
3-down is IMAGE, and a pic is a picture or image

explanation.surface: Something dodgy sits between the band Texas and The Commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: Texas and The Commitments look like the band and the film. '3' points to 3-down, IMAGE, synonym PIC. Texas is a state (S) of the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shady arouses suspicion of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Red fibre

definitions.meaning: a red property on the London Monopoly board

explanation.definitionFit: This London street belongs to Monopoly's red group; a thread is a single filament of fibre.

clue.text: Virgin taken into consideration

parts.note: into is in, the piece goes first
tact is consideration for others' feelings

explanation.surface: A virgin is taken into consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin forest is untouched and unspoilt.

clue.text: Orange tint with severe winds

indicators.note: winds means twists, so the letters wind into a new order

explanation.surface: An orange tint appears in the sky with severe winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' rearranges TINT SEVERE. VINE STREET is an orange property on the London Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly sets are named by colour, and this West End street is in the orange group.

clue.text: Make yourself small in place where you shouldn't be

explanation.definitionFit: To crouch is to sit on one's heels; an occupied empty building is lived in illegally.

clue.text: Honest post

explanation.definitionFit: An upstanding person is honest; a vertical post stands straight.

clue.text: I wait endlessly among political extremists for a drink

indicators.note: among means the middle pieces go in between the extremists

parts.note: left and right, L and R, are the political extremes
taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the wait word is dropped

parts.note: to queue is to wait in line

explanation.surface: Someone waits endlessly among political extremists to get a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from the wait word, and 'among' places the I and the trimmed wait between left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur is a sweet strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Some movement in knocker on door

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something moves inside the knocker on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical movement with a recurring theme, often the finale of a sonata.

clue.text: Republic's sacrifice has taken me away from superpower

definitions.note: the possessive reads as 'Republic is', a link

parts.note: the cost is what is sacrificed

indicators.note: 'taken me away' means those letters are removed

parts.note: America is the world superpower

explanation.surface: A republic resents the sacrifice the superpower has extracted from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken ... away from' removes ME from AMERICA to leave ARICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American republic.
